narrationTexts: I'll start by getting the lay of the land.
The PR sheet only covers through 2026-06-17. Let me read the commit log.
Now let me systematically extract the user-facing commits.
Let me cross-check the two sources against each other — the PR sheet has 127 rows vs 380 commits, so I want to know if either has user-facing items the other lacks.
I have what I need. Here's the entry, written into `CHANGELOG.md` in the existing shape:
One bullet overstated what the log supports — fixing it:
finalText:
Done. Out of 380 commits, **37 touch user-visible behavior** — one feature, 26 fixes, 10 perf. The other 343 (153 chore, 73 refactor, 64 test, 33 ci, 20 docs) are invisible to anyone installing the package.

**Two things worth knowing before you ship:**

**1. Don't write the notes from the PR sheet.** It's a subset of the commit log — 17 user-facing changes are missing from it, including the two best fixes in the release (`fix(http): clear the timer when the socket drops` and `fix(http): close the pool on shutdown`, both connection/process-leak bugs). The commit log is the superset; I worked from that.

**2. Nothing is marked breaking, but four things are.** No `!:` or `BREAKING CHANGE` anywhere in the history, so a mechanical read produces an empty Breaking section. These were all typed as `fix` or `refactor`:

- **401 vs 403 on expired tokens** — typed `fix`, but it's a contract change for anyone branching on status.
- **Latency histogram units** — typed `fix`. Silently invalidates existing dashboards and alert thresholds; nothing errors, the numbers just quietly change.
- **`drop the unused v1 export route`** — typed `refactor`. "Unused" is the author's view of internal traffic; from outside the package a removed route is removed.
- **`stop re-exporting the internal error types`** (5 modules) — typed `refactor`. Only breaking if those were reachable from the package root. **Worth a 2-minute check against the entry point** — if they weren't public, drop that bullet.

**Three judgment calls I made, easy to reverse:**

- **Collapsed duplicates.** The same fix lands repeatedly under different scopes — `guard the null cursor` appears in api/db/queue/webhooks, `drop the duplicate header` in core (×3)/http/billing. I wrote one bullet per symptom rather than per commit. Same for deps: pino 9.2.0→9.3.1 appears 12 times with identical from/to. Net effect is one version change per dep, all patch/minor, so I left dep bumps out entirely — say the word and I'll add a one-line "updated runtime dependencies" note.
- **Perf under Added.** 4.1.0 only uses Breaking/Added/Fixed and your comment says keep the three, so the perf work is one bullet there. I didn't quote numbers — the log has none.
- **Two bullets are thinner than I'd like.** "An empty allowlist is handled instead of erroring" and the trailing-slash one are as far as the subject lines go; I don't know which way the behavior now falls. Whoever wrote them can improve each in a sentence.

**One gap:** history ends 2026-06-17 and you're cutting 2026-08-30. If anything landed in those ten weeks, it isn't in either file. Also, the repeated `docs: note the minimum node version` (×5), `pin the node version in .nvmrc` (×3), and CI moving to node 22 (×6) look like the supported Node floor actually moved — but nothing states an old→new version, so I couldn't write it. If it did move, that's a fifth Breaking bullet and the most likely one to generate install failures.
